# Blueprint

> Blueprint helps a business turn one recurring task into a scoped, funded, measurable robot pilot and decide what happens afterward.

Show Blueprint one recurring task, including phone footage and rough economics. An approved budget is not required to start. Blueprint checks fit and uses free, bounded evaluation when it improves the decision. The site sees anonymized candidate results; each team sees its own results. A promising team and site may then approve a private introduction. The provider confirms its configuration, scope, price, availability, and site conditions before the customer sees one itemized proposal with the provider price plus Blueprint's scoped fee. The site approves the total before paid work. The provider or integrator installs and operates the robot; Blueprint coordinates the agreed plan and measures the physical outcome. Simulation is not physical proof or a deployment guarantee.

## Public pages

- [Home](https://tryblueprint.io/)
- [How it works](https://tryblueprint.io/how-it-works)
- [Discuss your site](https://tryblueprint.io/contact/site-operator)
- [Robot teams: apply for early access](https://tryblueprint.io/contact/robot-team)
- [Privacy](https://tryblueprint.io/privacy)
- [Terms](https://tryblueprint.io/terms)

Robot teams join by early access. Approved teams see only task cards sites chose to share. Invited evaluations are free within a bounded scope and carry no supplier commission. A provider confirms its site-specific pilot offer before it is shown as available. The site pays the provider's quoted price plus Blueprint's separately scoped fee if it accepts the pilot; the parties may invoice separately. Optional self-directed runs cost $99 per policy entry from a prepaid balance and retain their no-later-supplier-commission promise. Blueprint sets the run size. Pricing: https://tryblueprint.io/pricing. Contact: hello@tryblueprint.io.

## Evidence boundary

A Task Evaluation Run returns a decision or abstention. Pipeline owns method qualification and routing; physical outcomes remain distinct from simulation and generated evidence.

## Agent interfaces and compatibility

Current public/request tools are `blueprint.siteWorld.search`, `blueprint.catalog.search`, `blueprint.ask`, `blueprint.request.locationDraft`, `blueprint.siteWorld.get`, and `blueprint.siteWorld.launchReadiness`.

The historical read and hosted-session compatibility tools are `blueprint.commerce.order.get`, `blueprint.commerce.liveOrder.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlement.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlementReadiness`, `blueprint.session.create`, `blueprint.session.reset`, `blueprint.session.step`, `blueprint.session.runBatch`, `blueprint.session.control`, `blueprint.session.renderExplorer`, and `blueprint.session.export`. Historical availability does not make these current standalone products.

The team-scoped tools act for one robot team rather than reading the public catalogue, and are authenticated with a revocable per-team agent key rather than a person's session: `blueprint.team.me`, `blueprint.team.checkpoint.register`, `blueprint.team.checkpoint.list`, `blueprint.team.plan`, `blueprint.team.runs.start`, `blueprint.team.runs.release`, `blueprint.team.policy.get`, and `blueprint.team.policy.set`. Only `blueprint.team.runs.start` spends, it requires `confirm: true` with an idempotency key, and it is bounded by the daily and per-run limits the team sets. Runs are ranked by expected information gain per dollar rather than by likelihood of passing, so a run confirming what a team already knows ranks last. Planning, dry runs, funding and runs require the team's key to be connected to a verified Blueprint account whose email is approved for early access; that account issues and revokes the team's agent keys under Settings → Agent access. Until then those calls answer 403 `early_access_required`.

Truth labels are `capture_grounded`, `provider_derived`, `generated`, `request_gated`, `protected_robot_team`, `legacy_commerce_read_only`, and `decision_or_abstention`.
